<!-- EDIT: say what this analysis is for: which treatment decision, which two
     arms, and which outcome. Replace this comment with that text. -->

A `vt-fit` job builds virtual twins. A forest is grown on each arm alone, and
every patient is then predicted under **both** arms: the arm they received
and the one they did not. That gives each patient two predicted survival
curves, one per arm. The difference in restricted mean survival time (RMST) to
`HORIZON` between the two curves is the patient's estimated effect of the
treatment.

A patient's twin curve for the arm they did not receive is an extrapolation
from patients who did. Where no such patients resemble them, the prediction
says nothing, so the job also judges eligibility: which patients have
comparable patients in the other arm.

This template is **in flight**: it is built from one study, and a second study
running it through to `vt-explain` is what moves it to shipped.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: asis
SUBJECT <- "dead"
TYPE    <- "vt"
.in <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(randomForestSRC)
  library(cluster)
  library(hvtiRpropensity)
  library(hvtiPlotR)
  library(hvtiRutilities)
})
# One thread, so a fit reproduces from machine to machine. Left unset,
# randomForestSRC runs on every core its OpenMP build can see, and the forests
# changed with the thread count with every seed held fixed.
options(rf.cores = 1L, mc.cores = 1L)
# The versions this template was verified against on 2026-10-22. Below them a
# call here can fail or change meaning, and the message would arrive mid-render
# rather than here.
for (.floor in list(c("randomForestSRC", "3.7.0"), c("hvtiRpropensity", "0.2.0"))) {
  if (utils::packageVersion(.floor[1]) < .floor[2]) {
    stop("This job needs ", .floor[1], " >= ", .floor[2], "; ", utils::packageVersion(.floor[1]),
         " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
  }
}
# 2.8.20 for hv_group_palette(), which colors the observed-against-expected figure.
if (utils::packageVersion("hvtiPlotR") < "2.8.20") {
  stop("This job needs hvtiPlotR >= 2.8.20 for hv_group_palette(); ", utils::packageVersion("hvtiPlotR"),
       " is installed.\nUpdate it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
}
# The study root is the nearest directory above this file holding _study.yml,
# so the job renders the same from the Render button, quarto render, or
# render_job(), at any depth, with no path in this document to edit.
# Without the guard in .job_setup(), an unedited job renders green over a
# meaningless analysis. Here that is a fit of the template's placeholder
# arms and outcome, whose tables look exactly like a result.
# To render a job you have not finished, leave a chunk out with the chunk
# option skip, giving the reason in quotes, or call hvtiRtemplates::stop_here()
# in a chunk to leave out everything below it. A draft lists each one in a
# callout; a final render refuses them, as it refuses an unresolved marker.
# ?stop_here has more.
.job <- hvtiRtemplates:::.job_setup(SUBJECT, TYPE, envir = environment())
.root <- .job$root
set_path <- .job$set_path
.provenance_data <- list()
# Saves a figure as <name>.png, .pdf and .tiff in this set's graphs/ folder (or `kind`'s),
# under the SAVE_FIGURES and FIGURES study choices.
save_figure <- function(plot, name, width = 6, height = 4, kind = "graphs", linked = FALSE) {
  hvtiRtemplates:::.save_figure(plot, set_path(kind, paste0(name, ".png")), width, height,
                                SAVE_FIGURES, FIGURES, linked)
}

# The draft banners, if any, and the box under the title, after all the code above.
.job$notice
```

## Study choices

Edit these values for this study before rendering.

```{r}
#| label: edit-study-choices
DATASET <- "study"                          # EDIT: the dataset, as named in _study.yml.
ANALYSIS_SET <- NULL
WHERE <- NULL
ID <- "ccfid"                               # EDIT: the patient identifier.
KEY <- NULL

# Optional, and needs no edit: NULL reads the cohort alone. To join one
# registered ancillary dataset (labs, echoes), name it in JOIN. The cohort
# above decides the patients, one row each; the joined records of other
# patients are dropped and counted in the data table.
#   JOIN_VARS: the cohort columns each joined row carries; NULL carries all.
#   REDUCE: NULL keeps a row per joined record; list(rule = "first", by = "date")
#     keeps one row per patient. This job models one row per
#     patient, so a JOIN without REDUCE stops here.
#   JOIN_KEY: overrides the joined dataset's registered key.
JOIN <- NULL
JOIN_VARS <- NULL
REDUCE <- NULL
JOIN_KEY <- NULL
TIME <- "iv_dead"                           # EDIT: follow-up time.
STATUS <- "dead"                            # EDIT: the event, coded 0/1.
ARM <- "treatment"                          # EDIT: the treatment arm.
# EDIT: the two arms, in the order the difference is taken: a positive diff
# favors ARMS[1].
ARMS <- c("arm1", "arm2")
# EDIT: rows that received neither arm are predicted under both and fit by
# neither. NULL treats a missing ARM as no arm; a vector of levels names them.
NO_ARM <- NULL
# EDIT: a vp-fit set ("<subject>-<type>") whose selected set the forests use,
# or NULL to use PREDICTORS. The screen must not have seen the arm: that is what
# makes it treatment-blind, and this job checks it.
VP_SET <- NULL
PREDICTORS <- c("age", "sex")               # EDIT: used when VP_SET is NULL.
# EDIT: anything measured after the treatment decision. A screen does not know
# when a variable was measured, and a later procedure flag predicts the outcome
# because it is part of the path to it.
EXCLUDE <- character()
# EDIT: eligibility methods, one or more of "gower", "sid" and "isolation". "sid"
# reads the SID distance of the sid set named in SID_SET. "isolation" grows an
# isolation forest (the isotree package) on each arm: Gower asks whether the arm
# holds a patient like this one, the forest whether the arm rarely produces this
# combination of values. They catch different kinds of unusual.
ELIGIBILITY <- "gower"
# EDIT: "any" flags a patient any method flags, so with two methods a patient is
# eligible only when both keep them; "all" flags only when every method does. To
# decide by one method alone, name only that one in ELIGIBILITY.
COMBINE <- "any"
SID_SET <- NULL                             # EDIT: a sid set ("<subject>-<type>") when ELIGIBILITY has "sid".
# EDIT: the isolation-forest cutoff, a quantile of the arm's own cross-fitted
# scores. A patient the arm's forest isolates more readily than this share of
# the arm's own patients is flagged. There is no "largest" as with Gower: the
# arm's single most unusual score is mostly noise from the random cuts. The 95th
# and 99.5th percentiles are reported beside it.
ISOLATION_CUTOFF <- 0.99
# EDIT: when one arm's ages were capped for de-identification (HIPAA caps at
# 90), the age column and the cap, as one named number: c(age = 90). Both arms
# are capped, so an uncapped 95 does not look out of range against an arm that
# can only say 90. NULL leaves ages as read.
AGE_CAP <- NULL
# EDIT: the variables eligibility is judged on, or NULL to use the forests'
# predictors. Eligibility asks whether an arm holds patients like this one in
# what the treatment acts on, which need not be what predicts death: a repair
# chosen by anatomy can be judged on the anatomy alone, while the forests still
# adjust for everything else. Set here, these drive the Gower distance and the
# propensity comparison; a sid set keeps the variables it was clustered on.
ELIGIBILITY_VARS <- NULL
# EDIT: the fewest events per candidate feature an arm's forest may have before
# the report is marked draft (a final render stops). 20 is a guess, the low end
# of a 20 to 30 rule of thumb with no study behind it; 0 reports the ratio only.
MIN_EVENTS_PER_FEATURE <- 20
# EDIT: graded predictors coded as numbers (a 0 to 3 degree, say). The Gower
# distance ranks them, so 0 against 3 is farther than 0 against 1; unnamed, every
# mismatched grade counts the same. Names the predictors do not include are ignored.
ORDINAL <- character()
# EDIT: "na.impute" imputes missing predictors inside each forest; "na.omit"
# drops the patient. The outcome is required either way.
NA_ACTION <- "na.impute"
# EDIT: for stacked multiple imputations, the column numbering them. This
# release uses one completed dataset, IMPUTATION_USE; pooling is not done.
IMPUTATION <- NULL
IMPUTATION_USE <- 1L
# EDIT: the RMST horizon, in TIME's units. Keep it inside the follow-up of both
# arms; past the last follow-up every curve is cut at the same place and the
# difference means nothing. This job stops if it is not.
HORIZON <- 4
# The observed-against-expected test follows each patient to TAU at most. NULL
# takes the shorter of the two arms' follow-up, the furthest both forests have
# data for; past it a forest's cumulative hazard is held at its last step.
TAU <- NULL
# EDIT: the level of the observed-against-expected interval. 95% because the
#       test's p-value is read against 0.05, and a reader takes an interval
#       beside a p-value for 95%. The Kaplan-Meier above is 70%; the level is
#       printed beside every interval either way.
TEST_LEVEL <- 0.95
# How many patients' curves the spaghetti figure draws per panel. More than
# that are thinned to patients spaced evenly through the ranking of predicted
# survival, so the drawn lines keep the cohort's spread and need no seed.
SPAGHETTI_N <- 200
NTREE <- 1000                              # EDIT: trees per arm forest.
NSPLIT <- 8
SEED <- 1024                                # EDIT: part of every cache key.
# Set TRUE after changing a choice above. A cache whose inputs changed stops the
# render instead of returning the old result; TRUE recomputes only the caches
# that are out of date.
REFIT <- FALSE

# Each figure is saved to graphs/ as a PNG (for Word) and a PDF (for the publisher), and as a TIFF when ragg is installed.
# SAVE_FIGURES <- FALSE saves none; FIGURES keeps only the figures whose names
# start with one of its entries, e.g. FIGURES <- c("vt-fit-km"). The names are the
# file names, listed for each template in the templates README.
SAVE_FIGURES <- TRUE
FIGURES <- NULL
```

## Cohort

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "The data this job read"
# The checksum of every dataset in manifest.yaml is checked before anything is
# read, so a result can name the data that produced it. It stops on a mismatch.
hvtiRutilities::verify_manifest(file.path(.root, "manifest.yaml"))
.cfg <- study_config(start = .root)
# Stacked imputations repeat each patient once per imputation, so a row is unique on the ID and the imputation.
if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) KEY <- unique(c(if (is.null(KEY)) ID else KEY, IMPUTATION))
job_data <- hvtiRtemplates::read_job_data(.cfg, dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET,
                                          where = WHERE, id = ID, key = KEY, join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS,
                                          reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY, one_row_per_patient = TRUE,
                                          imputation = IMPUTATION)
d <- job_data$data
.provenance_data <- c(if (exists(".provenance_data")) .provenance_data else list(), list(job_data$provenance),
                      if (!is.null(job_data$provenance_join)) list(job_data$provenance_join))
knitr::kable(job_data$record, col.names = c("Data", ""))
if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) {
  IMPUTATION <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")$imputation
  .m <- length(unique(d[[IMPUTATION]]))
  if (!IMPUTATION_USE %in% d[[IMPUTATION]]) {
    stop("IMPUTATION_USE = ", IMPUTATION_USE, " is not an imputation in ", IMPUTATION, ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  d <- d[d[[IMPUTATION]] == IMPUTATION_USE, setdiff(names(d), IMPUTATION), drop = FALSE]
  cat("This job uses imputation ", IMPUTATION_USE, " of ", .m, ". The forests are not pooled across imputations.\n",
      sep = "")
}
# read_job_data() matches ID case-insensitively and falls back from ccfid to an
# MRN, without changing ID here. Take the name it resolved.
ID <- attr(job_data$record, "selection")$id
# This job saves one row per patient (vt.rds), and a sid set joins on it. No
# saved artifact holds a raw identifier, an MRN least of all (#203), so the ID
# is replaced here by its digest under the study's key, the form a sid set
# saves too. Everything below, and everything saved, carries only the digest.
.id_key <- hvtiRtemplates:::.study_id_key(.root)
d[[ID]] <- hvtiRtemplates:::.id_digest(d[[ID]], .id_key)
.no_arm <- if (is.null(NO_ARM)) is.na(d[[ARM]]) else d[[ARM]] %in% NO_ARM
.treated <- d[[ARM]] %in% ARMS
.other <- !.no_arm & !.treated
if (any(.other)) {
  stop(sum(.other), " row(s) have an ARM that is neither in ARMS nor NO_ARM: ",
       paste(unique(d[[ARM]][.other]), collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
}
# Arms are names, never positions. A numeric ARM (0 and 1) would otherwise index
# the lists of forests by position, so ARMS and the arm column become text once,
# here, and every list below is keyed by that text. A missing arm stays NA.
ARMS <- as.character(ARMS)
d[[ARM]] <- as.character(d[[ARM]])
.no_outcome <- .treated & (is.na(d[[TIME]]) | is.na(d[[STATUS]]))
if (any(.no_outcome)) {
  stop(sum(.no_outcome), " treated patient(s) have no outcome. A forest cannot learn from them, and imputing one ",
       "would invent follow-up. Resolve them in the dataset build.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (!all(d[[STATUS]][.treated] %in% c(0, 1))) stop(STATUS, " must be coded 0 and 1.", call. = FALSE)
NA_ACTION <- match.arg(NA_ACTION, c("na.impute", "na.omit"))
# Run again after na.omit drops patients (predictors chunk): the guard must hold for the patients the forests see.
.arm_counts <- function(d, when = "") {
  counts <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {
    i <- d[[ARM]] %in% a
    data.frame(Arm = a, Patients = sum(i), Events = sum(d[[STATUS]][i] == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
  }))
  thin <- counts$Patients < 2 | counts$Events < 1
  if (any(thin)) {
    stop("Each arm needs at least 2 treated patients and 1 event", when, "; ",
         paste0(counts$Arm[thin], " has ", counts$Patients[thin], " patient(s) and ", counts$Events[thin], " event(s)",
                collapse = "; "), ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  counts
}
.counts <- .arm_counts(d)
.counts <- base::rbind(.counts, data.frame(Arm = "No arm", Patients = sum(.no_arm), Events = NA_integer_))
knitr::kable(.counts)
```

## Predictors

```{r}
#| label: predictors
.vp_read <- NULL
if (!is.null(VP_SET)) {
  .vp_path <- file.path(dirname(dirname(set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))), VP_SET, "vp.rds")
  if (!file.exists(.vp_path)) stop("No vp-fit screen at ", .vp_path, ". Render that job first.", call. = FALSE)
  .vp_read <- hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(.vp_path, "screen", .cfg, "the vp-fit job")
  if (tolower(ARM) %in% tolower(.vp_read$value$coverage$variable)) {
    stop("The screen in ", VP_SET, " was given ", ARM, " as a candidate, so it is not treatment-blind. ",
         "Re-run vp-fit without the arm.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  .predictors <- .vp_read$value$selected
  .provenance_data <- c(.provenance_data, .vp_read$lineage$data)
} else {
  .predictors <- PREDICTORS
}
.predictors <- setdiff(.predictors, EXCLUDE)
.leaks <- intersect(tolower(.predictors), tolower(c(ARM, TIME, STATUS, ID)))
if (length(.leaks)) {
  stop("PREDICTORS (or the screen) includes the arm, outcome or ID: ", paste(.leaks, collapse = ", "), ".",
       call. = FALSE)
}
.missing <- setdiff(.predictors, names(d))
if (length(.missing)) stop("Not in the data this job read: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
if (!length(.predictors)) stop("No predictors are left after EXCLUDE.", call. = FALSE)
.elig_vars <- if (is.null(ELIGIBILITY_VARS)) .predictors else ELIGIBILITY_VARS
.leaks <- intersect(tolower(.elig_vars), tolower(c(ARM, TIME, STATUS, ID, EXCLUDE)))
if (length(.leaks)) {
  stop("ELIGIBILITY_VARS includes the arm, outcome, ID or an EXCLUDE column: ", paste(.leaks, collapse = ", "), ".",
       call. = FALSE)
}
.missing <- setdiff(.elig_vars, names(d))
if (length(.missing)) stop("ELIGIBILITY_VARS not in the data: ", paste(.missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
if (!is.null(AGE_CAP)) {
  if (!is.numeric(AGE_CAP) || length(AGE_CAP) != 1L || !is.finite(AGE_CAP) || is.null(names(AGE_CAP)) ||
        !names(AGE_CAP) %in% names(d) || !is.numeric(d[[names(AGE_CAP)]])) {
    stop("AGE_CAP must be one named number, a numeric age column and its cap, e.g. c(age = 90).", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # Capping the follow-up time would truncate it with the event left as recorded.
  if (tolower(names(AGE_CAP)) %in% tolower(c(ID, ARM, TIME, STATUS))) {
    stop("AGE_CAP names ", names(AGE_CAP), ", the ID, arm or outcome; name the age column.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  .age <- names(AGE_CAP)
  .capped <- !is.na(d[[.age]]) & d[[.age]] > AGE_CAP
  cat(sum(.capped), " patient(s) with ", .age, " above ", AGE_CAP, " capped at ", AGE_CAP, " (AGE_CAP), in every arm.\n",
      sep = "")
  d[[.age]] <- pmin(d[[.age]], unname(AGE_CAP))
}
.chr <- union(.predictors, .elig_vars)
.chr <- .chr[vapply(d[.chr], is.character, logical(1L))]
d[.chr] <- lapply(d[.chr], factor)
if (NA_ACTION == "na.omit") {
  .kept <- stats::complete.cases(d[.predictors])
  cat(sum(!.kept), "patient(s) missing a predictor were dropped (NA_ACTION = \"na.omit\").\n")
  d <- d[.kept, , drop = FALSE]
  invisible(.arm_counts(d, " after NA_ACTION = \"na.omit\" dropped patients"))
  .no_arm <- .no_arm[.kept]
  .treated <- .treated[.kept]
}
# Every column read, kept for explaining a sid set's flags: its variables are known only once the set is read.
.d_read <- d
d <- d[, c(ID, ARM, TIME, STATUS, union(.predictors, .elig_vars)), drop = FALSE]
cat("Predictors:", paste(.predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (!is.null(ELIGIBILITY_VARS)) cat("Eligibility variables:", paste(.elig_vars, collapse = ", "), "\n")
# Each arm's forest is grown on that arm alone, so each arm's events are what its splits have.
.epf <- hvtiRtemplates:::.check_events_per_feature(
  vapply(ARMS, function(a) sum(d[[STATUS]][d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated] == 1), numeric(1L)),
  length(.predictors), MIN_EVENTS_PER_FEATURE
)
cat("Events per candidate feature:",
    paste0(.epf$group, " ", .epf$events_per_feature, " (", .epf$events, " events)", collapse = "; "), "\n")
```

## The observed outcome

What happened in each arm, before any model: Kaplan-Meier, with 70% confidence limits (about one standard
error). The twins below predict each patient under both arms, so this is the check that each arm's
follow-up reaches the horizon with patients still at risk. An arm with few at risk at `HORIZON` carries a
twin curve there that rests on little data.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-km
#| tbl-cap: "Each arm's observed outcome: patients, events, and Kaplan-Meier survival at the horizon with
#|   70% confidence limits"
.km_data <- d[.treated, c(TIME, STATUS, ARM), drop = FALSE]
.km_data[[ARM]] <- factor(.km_data[[ARM]], levels = ARMS)
.km_data[[STATUS]] <- as.integer(.km_data[[STATUS]])
.km_times <- sort(unique(c(pretty(c(0, max(.km_data[[TIME]]))), HORIZON)))
.km <- hvtiPlotR::hv_survival(.km_data, time_col = TIME, event_col = STATUS, group_col = ARM, conf_level = 0.70,
                              report_times = .km_times)
.km_at <- .km$tables$report[.km$tables$report$report_time == HORIZON, , drop = FALSE]
# The number at risk comes from the risk table the figure draws, so table and figure agree; the report
# table's own n.risk is survfit's, counted just before the time, and can differ by a patient.
.km_risk <- .km$tables$risk[.km$tables$risk$report_time == HORIZON, , drop = FALSE]
.km_tbl <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {
  x <- .km_data[.km_data[[ARM]] == a, , drop = FALSE]
  h <- .km_at[as.character(.km_at$strata) == a, , drop = FALSE]
  k <- .km_risk$n.risk[as.character(.km_risk$strata) == a]
  data.frame(arm = a, patients = nrow(x), events = sum(x[[STATUS]] == 1L), last_follow_up = max(x[[TIME]]),
             at_risk = if (length(k)) k else 0L, survival = if (nrow(h)) h$surv else NA_real_,
             lower = if (nrow(h)) h$lower else NA_real_, upper = if (nrow(h)) h$upper else NA_real_)
}))
names(.km_tbl)[5:8] <- paste0(c("at_risk", "survival", "lower", "upper"), "_", HORIZON)
knitr::kable(.km_tbl, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-km
#| fig-cap: "Kaplan-Meier survival in each arm, with 70% confidence limits and the numbers at risk. The
#|   dashed line is the RMST horizon."
.fig <- plot(.km) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = HORIZON, linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Time", y = "Survival (%)", color = "Arm", fill = "Arm") +
  hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) +
  # The house theme drops the legend; two arms need it to tell the curves apart.
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
.fig <- hvtiPlotR::hv_atrisk_compose(.fig, hvtiPlotR::hv_atrisk(.km))
save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-km", height = 5)
.fig
```

## Eligibility

A patient's twin curve for the arm they did not receive is only as good as the
patients it was learned from. **Out of distribution** means a patient has no
close counterpart in an arm, so that arm's forest would be extrapolating for
them. The rule is the same for every distance this job can use. For each arm,
each patient's nearest neighbor in that arm (never themself) is compared with
the largest nearest-neighbor distance among the arm's own patients. That
reference is the arm's own largest gap: a patient farther from the arm than its
own members are from each other is outside what the arm covers. A treated
patient is judged against the other arm; a patient with no arm is judged against
both and must pass both.

The isolation forest (`"isolation"` in `ELIGIBILITY`) asks the same question
by a different route. It grows random trees on one arm's patients, each split
on one variable at a random cut, until a patient stands alone. A patient the
arm rarely produces, an odd mix of values, stands alone after few cuts and
scores high. The arm's own patients are scored cross-fitted, in five folds, each
by the forest grown on the other four, because a forest isolates a patient it was
grown on more easily and an in-sample reference would set the line too high. A
judged patient is dealt one of the five folds too and scored by that fold's
forest, so both sides are scored the same way: by one forest, grown on four
fifths of the arm, that never saw them. The line is `ISOLATION_CUTOFF`, a quantile of the arm's own scores.

Patients are **flagged, not dropped**. The flags are saved with the fit and the
effect estimates carry them, so a report can show the effect with and without
the flagged patients.

```{r}
#| label: ood
# One rule, applied to any patient-by-patient distance. For each arm, each
# patient's nearest neighbor in that arm (never themself) is compared with the
# largest nearest-neighbor distance among the arm's own patients. Farther than
# that, STRICTLY, and the arm's forest would be extrapolating. A treated patient
# is judged against the other arm; a row with no arm against both.
#
# A distance can be unavailable: Gower gives NA for two patients who share no
# observed predictor. An unavailable distance is no evidence of nearness, so it
# counts as infinitely far. A patient with no finite distance to any patient in
# an arm has no comparable neighbor there and is out of distribution for it,
# with that reason; an arm member with no finite within-arm neighbor does not
# set the arm's reference. Every judged patient therefore gets TRUE or FALSE,
# never NA.
vt_ood <- function(dist, ids, arm, arms) {
  dist <- as.matrix(dist)[ids, ids, drop = FALSE]
  dist[is.na(dist)] <- Inf
  diag(dist) <- Inf
  rows <- lapply(arms, function(a) {
    members <- which(arm %in% a)
    nn_within <- apply(dist[members, members, drop = FALSE], 1L, min)
    nn_within <- nn_within[is.finite(nn_within)]
    # An arm whose members have no finite neighbor has no reference gap, so nobody can be shown
    # to sit inside it: they are flagged with that reason, and the eligibility chunk stops on it.
    reference <- if (length(nn_within)) max(nn_within) else NA_real_
    judged <- which(is.na(arm) | !arm %in% c(a, NA))
    if (!length(judged)) return(NULL)
    sub <- dist[judged, members, drop = FALSE]
    nn <- apply(sub, 1L, which.min)
    distance <- sub[cbind(seq_along(judged), nn)]
    none <- !is.finite(distance)
    out <- none | is.na(reference) | distance > reference
    reason <- ifelse(none, sprintf("no comparable %s patient (no predictor observed in common)", a), "")
    if (is.na(reference)) {
      reason[!none] <- sprintf("arm %s has no reference gap", a)
    } else {
      reason[out & !none] <- sprintf("nearest %s patient at %.3f, beyond that arm's largest gap %.3f",
                                     a, distance[out & !none], reference)
    }
    data.frame(ID = ids[judged], method = NA_character_, arm = a, nn_id = ifelse(none, NA, ids[members][nn]),
               distance = distance, reference = reference,
               ratio = if (length(nn_within)) distance / stats::median(nn_within) else NA_real_,
               in_distribution = !out, reason = reason)
  })
  do.call(base::rbind, rows)
}

# Gower over the eligibility variables only (the model predictors unless
# ELIGIBILITY_VARS names others): mixed types, no model, bounded in [0, 1].
# A 0/1 column is declared symmetric binary. daisy() would otherwise treat it as
# interval scaled, which gives the same distance, and warn in every report.
# daisy() scores any mismatch of an unordered factor as 1, so a grade of 0
# against 3 would count the same as 0 against 1. The `ordinal` predictors become
# ordered factors, levels sorted by their numeric codes, which daisy ranks and
# scales to [0, 1]. Only the distance sees this; the forests keep the data as read.
vt_elig_gower <- function(d, predictors, id, ordinal = character()) {
  x <- d[predictors]
  for (v in intersect(ordinal, predictors)) {
    lv <- levels(factor(x[[v]]))
    num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(lv))
    if (anyNA(num)) {
      stop("ORDINAL predictor ", v, " has levels that are not numeric codes: ", paste(lv[is.na(num)], collapse = ", "),
           ".", call. = FALSE)
    }
    x[[v]] <- factor(as.character(x[[v]]), levels = lv[order(num)], ordered = TRUE)
  }
  binary <- predictors[vapply(x, function(col) {
    col <- stats::na.omit(col)
    is.numeric(col) && length(unique(col)) == 2L && all(col %in% c(0, 1))
  }, logical(1L))]
  m <- as.matrix(cluster::daisy(x, metric = "gower", type = if (length(binary)) list(symm = binary) else list()))
  dimnames(m) <- list(d[[id]], d[[id]])
  m
}

# Which predictors put an out-of-distribution patient outside the arm they were
# judged against: a number outside the range the arm's patients span, or a level
# that at most `rare` of them share. A distance says how far; this says why, in
# terms a clinician can check against the chart. At most `n` are named; a patient
# with none is unusual only in combination.
vt_ood_features <- function(out_rows, d, id, arm_of, predictors, n = 3L, rare = 2L) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(out_rows)), function(i) {
    p <- d[match(out_rows$ID[i], d[[id]]), , drop = FALSE]
    members <- d[arm_of %in% out_rows$arm[i], , drop = FALSE]
    why <- character()
    for (v in predictors) {
      a <- p[[v]]
      u <- members[[v]]
      if (is.na(a)) next
      if (is.numeric(u) && !all(stats::na.omit(u) %in% c(0, 1))) {
        rg <- range(u, na.rm = TRUE)
        if (a < rg[1] || a > rg[2]) {
          why <- c(why, sprintf("%s %s outside %s's range [%s, %s]", v, format(signif(a, 3)), out_rows$arm[i],
                                format(signif(rg[1], 3)), format(signif(rg[2], 3))))
        }
      } else {
        k <- sum(as.character(u) == as.character(a), na.rm = TRUE)
        if (k <= rare) why <- c(why, sprintf("%s = %s (%d of %d in %s)", v, as.character(a), k, nrow(members), out_rows$arm[i]))
      }
    }
    if (!length(why)) "none alone; unusual in combination" else paste(utils::head(why, n), collapse = "; ")
  }, character(1L))
}

# Each method's flags explained by the variables that method's distance used:
# the eligibility set for Gower, the sid set's own for SID. Explaining a SID flag
# by variables the distance never saw would name a cause it did not have, so
# when a method's variables are unknown or absent from the data, say so.
vt_flag_features <- function(out_rows, d, id, arm_of, vars_by_method) {
  out <- character(nrow(out_rows))
  for (m in unique(out_rows$method)) {
    at <- which(out_rows$method == m)
    vars <- vars_by_method[[m]]
    absent <- setdiff(vars, names(d))
    out[at] <- if (!length(vars)) {
      sprintf("not computed: the %s set records no variables", m)
    } else if (length(absent)) {
      sprintf("not computed: %s used %s, not in this job's data", m, paste(absent, collapse = ", "))
    } else {
      vt_ood_features(out_rows[at, , drop = FALSE], d, id, arm_of, vars)
    }
  }
  out
}

# The SID distance a sid job saved. Read, never refit, and refused when it does
# not cover every patient here.
# Returns the distance with the whole reader result as attribute "read", so the
# eligibility chunk can carry the sid set's record and lineage into vt.rds.
vt_elig_sid <- function(path, ids, cfg, key = NULL,
                        read = function(p) hvtiRtemplates:::.read_handoff(p, "SID fit", cfg, "the sid job")) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("No sid clustering at ", path, ". Render that job first.", call. = FALSE)
  got <- read(path)
  # A sid set's distance is labeled by ID digests under the study key, with the
  # key's fingerprint saved beside it. A different fingerprint means the key
  # changed since, and every digest would miss.
  if (!is.null(key) && !identical(got$value$id_key, hvtiRtemplates:::.id_key_fingerprint(key))) {
    stop("The sid set at ", path, " was digested under a different study key. Re-render it.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  m <- as.matrix(got$value$dist)
  absent <- setdiff(ids, rownames(m))
  if (length(absent)) {
    stop(length(absent), " patient(s) in this job are not in the sid distance at ", path, ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  structure(m[ids, ids, drop = FALSE], read = got)
}

# The isolation-forest judgment, in vt_ood()'s row shape so the methods combine
# alike: `distance` holds the score (higher is more unusual) and `reference` the
# arm's line, the `cutoff` quantile of its own scores. Each arm's patients are
# split into `folds` folds; a member is scored by the forest grown on the other
# folds. A judged patient is dealt a fold the same way and scored by that fold's
# forest alone, so both sides get one forest that never saw them, grown on the same
# share of the arm. A mean over all the forests would be a less noisy score than
# the one the line is a quantile of, and would be judged against the wrong line.
# Missing values are handled inside the trees. Returns the rows with the
# flag counts at each quantile in `sensitivity` as attribute "sensitivity".
vt_elig_isolation <- function(d, vars, ids, arm, arms, cutoff = 0.99, sensitivity = c(0.95, 0.995),
                              folds = 5L, seed = 1L, ntrees = 500L, sample_size = 256L) {
  if (!requireNamespace("isotree", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("ELIGIBILITY includes \"isolation\", which needs the isotree package. Install it, then re-render.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.numeric(cutoff) || length(cutoff) != 1L || is.na(cutoff) || cutoff <= 0 || cutoff >= 1) {
    stop("ISOLATION_CUTOFF must be one number between 0 and 1, such as 0.99.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  x <- d[vars]
  probs <- sort(unique(c(sensitivity, cutoff)))
  sens <- list()
  rows <- lapply(arms, function(a) {
    members <- which(arm %in% a)
    judged <- which(is.na(arm) | !arm %in% c(a, NA))
    if (!length(judged)) return(NULL)
    # Cross-fitting holds a fold out of each forest, and a forest needs two patients to grow on.
    if (length(members) < 3L) {
      stop("Arm ", a, " has ", length(members), " patient(s); the isolation forest needs at least 3. ",
           "Leave \"isolation\" out of ELIGIBILITY.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    k <- min(folds, length(members))
    set.seed(seed)
    fold <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(members)))
    fold_judged <- sample(rep_len(seq_len(k), length(judged)))
    own <- numeric(length(members))
    score <- numeric(length(judged))
    for (f in seq_len(k)) {
      train <- members[fold != f]
      fit <- isotree::isolation.forest(x[train, , drop = FALSE], ntrees = ntrees, ndim = 1L, nthreads = 1L,
                                       sample_size = min(sample_size, length(train)), seed = seed + f)
      own[fold == f] <- stats::predict(fit, x[members[fold == f], , drop = FALSE])
      if (any(fold_judged == f)) score[fold_judged == f] <- stats::predict(fit, x[judged[fold_judged == f], , drop = FALSE])
    }
    lines <- stats::quantile(own, probs, names = FALSE)
    reference <- lines[probs == cutoff]
    sens[[a]] <<- data.frame(arm = a, quantile = probs, cutoff = lines, judged = length(judged),
                             flagged = vapply(lines, function(l) sum(score > l), integer(1L)))
    out <- score > reference
    data.frame(ID = ids[judged], method = NA_character_, arm = a, nn_id = NA_character_, distance = score,
               reference = reference, ratio = score / stats::median(own), in_distribution = !out,
               reason = ifelse(out, sprintf("isolation score %.3f, above %s's %s quantile %.3f", score, a,
                                            format(cutoff), reference), ""))
  })
  structure(do.call(base::rbind, rows), sensitivity = do.call(base::rbind, unname(sens)))
}

# Eligible patients with a value the arm they were judged against never shows: a
# number outside the arm's observed range, or a level none of its patients has.
# Gower and the isolation forest each fold every variable into one number, so one extreme value
# among many can leave a patient eligible while the arm's forest extrapolates on
# that variable for them. They stay eligible; this lists them for review. `pairs`
# holds the ID and arm of each eligible patient's judgments.
vt_outside_range <- function(pairs, d, id, arm_of, vars) {
  hits <- lapply(vars, function(v) {
    do.call(base::rbind, lapply(unique(pairs$arm), function(a) {
      p <- pairs$ID[pairs$arm == a]
      x <- d[[v]][match(p, d[[id]])]
      u <- stats::na.omit(d[[v]][arm_of %in% a])
      if (!length(u)) return(NULL)
      # Binary is a property of the column, as in vt_elig_gower(), not of one arm's values.
      if (is.numeric(u) && !all(stats::na.omit(d[[v]]) %in% c(0, 1))) {
        rg <- range(u)
        side <- ifelse(x < rg[1], "below", ifelse(x > rg[2], "above", NA_character_))
        seen <- sprintf("[%s, %s]", format(signif(rg[1], 3)), format(signif(rg[2], 3)))
      } else {
        side <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & !as.character(x) %in% as.character(u), "a level not in the arm", NA_character_)
        seen <- paste(sort(unique(as.character(u))), collapse = ", ")
      }
      hit <- !is.na(side)
      if (!any(hit)) return(NULL)
      data.frame(ID = p[hit], arm = a, variable = v, value = as.character(x[hit]), side = side[hit], arm_values = seen)
    }))
  })
  out <- do.call(base::rbind, hits)
  if (is.null(out)) {
    out <- data.frame(ID = character(), arm = character(), variable = character(), value = character(),
                      side = character(), arm_values = character())
  }
  out
}

# A patient is eligible when every arm they were judged against passed, per
# method; then methods combine: "any" flag excludes, or "all" must.
vt_combine <- function(rows, combine = c("any", "all")) {
  combine <- match.arg(combine)
  per <- stats::aggregate(in_distribution ~ ID + method, rows, all)
  flagged <- stats::aggregate(!in_distribution ~ ID, per, if (combine == "any") any else all)
  data.frame(ID = flagged$ID, elig = !flagged[[2]])
}

# How far eligibility rules overlap. `flags` holds one column per rule, TRUE
# where the patient is eligible and NA where the rule did not judge them;
# `group` is each patient's arm. Returns the count of patients under each exact
# set of flagging rules by group, with the rules that did not judge them named,
# and, for each pair of rules, their agreement
# over the patients both judged, with Cohen's kappa (NA when both rules give
# everyone the same answer, so chance agreement is total).
vt_overlap <- function(flags, group) {
  combo <- apply(flags, 1L, function(x) {
    hit <- names(flags)[!is.na(x) & !x]
    unjudged <- names(flags)[is.na(x)]
    paste0(if (length(hit)) paste(hit, collapse = " + ") else "none",
           if (length(unjudged)) paste0("; not judged by ", paste(unjudged, collapse = ", ")))
  })
  tab <- table(combo, group)
  combinations <- data.frame(flagged_by = rownames(tab), unclass(tab)[, , drop = FALSE], check.names = FALSE,
                             row.names = NULL)
  combinations <- combinations[order(!startsWith(combinations$flagged_by, "none"), combinations$flagged_by), , drop = FALSE]
  pairs <- if (ncol(flags) > 1L) {
    do.call(base::rbind, lapply(utils::combn(names(flags), 2L, simplify = FALSE), function(p) {
      a <- flags[[p[1]]]
      b <- flags[[p[2]]]
      ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b)
      a <- a[ok]
      b <- b[ok]
      po <- mean(a == b)
      pe <- mean(a) * mean(b) + mean(!a) * mean(!b)
      data.frame(rules = paste(p, collapse = " vs "), judged = sum(ok), both_eligible = sum(a & b),
                 both_flagged = sum(!a & !b), only_first = sum(!a & b), only_second = sum(a & !b),
                 kappa = if (sum(ok) && pe < 1) round((po - pe) / (1 - pe), 2) else NA_real_)
    }))
  }
  list(combinations = combinations, pairs = pairs)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: eligibility
.methods <- match.arg(ELIGIBILITY, c("gower", "sid", "isolation"), several.ok = TRUE)
.ids <- d[[ID]]
.arm <- ifelse(.no_arm, NA_character_, as.character(d[[ARM]]))
.sid_read <- NULL
.dist <- list(
  gower = function() vt_elig_gower(d, .elig_vars, ID, ORDINAL),
  sid = function() {
    if (is.null(SID_SET)) stop("ELIGIBILITY includes \"sid\"; name the sid set in SID_SET.", call. = FALSE)
    m <- vt_elig_sid(file.path(dirname(dirname(set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))), SID_SET, "sid.rds"), .ids, .cfg,
                     key = .id_key)
    # The sid set decided some flags, so its record and data lineage travel
    # into vt.rds with the vp screen's (see `save`).
    .sid_read <<- attr(m, "read")
    .provenance_data <<- c(.provenance_data, .sid_read$lineage$data)
    m
  }
)
.judged <- lapply(stats::setNames(.methods, .methods), function(m) {
  if (m == "isolation") return(vt_elig_isolation(d, .elig_vars, .ids, .arm, ARMS, cutoff = ISOLATION_CUTOFF, seed = SEED))
  vt_ood(.dist[[m]](), .ids, .arm, ARMS)
})
.iso_sens <- attr(.judged$isolation, "sensitivity")
.elig_rows <- do.call(base::rbind, unname(lapply(.methods, function(m) transform(.judged[[m]], method = m))))
if (anyNA(.elig_rows$reference)) {
  .bad <- unique(.elig_rows$method[is.na(.elig_rows$reference)])
  stop("An arm has no two patients with a finite distance by ", paste(.bad, collapse = ", "),
       ", so its reference gap is undefined. Check the predictors' missingness.", call. = FALSE)
}
.elig_rows$features <- ""
.ood_at <- which(!.elig_rows$in_distribution)
.sid_vars <- if (!is.null(.sid_read)) .sid_read$value$vars
.elig_rows$features[.ood_at] <- vt_flag_features(.elig_rows[.ood_at, ], .d_read, ID, .arm,
                                                 list(gower = .elig_vars, sid = .sid_vars, isolation = .elig_vars))
# With no finite distance there is no comparison to explain; vt_ood()'s reason says why.
.nofin <- .ood_at[!is.finite(.elig_rows$distance[.ood_at])]
.elig_rows$features[.nofin] <- .elig_rows$reason[.nofin]
.elig <- vt_combine(.elig_rows, COMBINE)
for (m in .methods) {
  .one <- vt_combine(.elig_rows[.elig_rows$method == m, ], "any")
  .elig[[paste0("elig_", m)]] <- .one$elig[match(.elig$ID, .one$ID)]
}
# The forests' predictors too, not only the eligibility set: when ELIGIBILITY_VARS
# leaves a predictor out, the arm's forest still extrapolates on it.
.outside <- vt_outside_range(unique(.elig_rows[.elig_rows$ID %in% .elig$ID[.elig$elig], c("ID", "arm")]), d, ID, .arm,
                             union(.predictors, .elig_vars))
# Sensitivity only, never part of the combined rule: forest propensity common support.
# ps_forest() refuses missing predictors, while the arm forests impute them
# (NA_ACTION = "na.impute"). So the propensity model gets a forest-imputed copy
# of the treated patients' predictors, seeded, and the arm forests keep the
# data as read. The arm is left out of the imputation, so the treatment does not
# shape the predictors that then predict it. Under "na.omit" nothing is missing and the copy equals d.
# Two propensity models when ELIGIBILITY_VARS is set, one otherwise. The
# common-support flag judges on the eligibility variables, as Gower does. The
# saved `ps` stays on the predictors, because vt-explain weights the betas with
# it, and weights from the eligibility set alone would leave the other
# confounders unbalanced.
# Each model imputes and fits on its own variables, so a column only the
# eligibility set names cannot change how the predictors are filled in, nor the
# saved model's scores.
vt_ps <- function(vars) {
  x <- d[.treated, c(ID, ARM, vars), drop = FALSE]
  if (anyNA(x[vars])) {
    imp <- x[vars]
    # impute() drops a patient who is missing every predictor, so the imputed
    # rows are matched back by ID (its row names), never by position.
    rownames(imp) <- x[[ID]]
    set.seed(SEED)
    imputed <- randomForestSRC::impute(data = imp, ntree = 100L, seed = -abs(SEED), verbose = FALSE)
    back <- match(x[[ID]], rownames(imputed))
    if (anyNA(back)) {
      cat(sum(is.na(back)), " treated patient(s) could not be scored for the propensity sensitivity ",
          "(no predictor observed); they are not eligible under it.\n", sep = "")
    }
    x <- x[!is.na(back), , drop = FALSE]
    x[vars] <- imputed[back[!is.na(back)], vars, drop = FALSE]
  }
  set.seed(SEED)
  # The propensity forest keeps its formula too, and reformulate() would tie it to this
  # environment (and the raw IDs in `job_data`); point it at the global environment.
  ps_forest(stats::reformulate(vars, ARM, env = globalenv()), data = x, treatment_col = ARM, id_col = ID,
            treated_level = ARMS[1], ntree = NTREE, seed = -abs(SEED))
}
.ps <- vt_ps(.predictors)
.ps_elig <- if (setequal(.elig_vars, .predictors)) .ps else vt_ps(.elig_vars)
# ps_support() adds weak_common (outside the range both arms occupy) to $data.
# Patients with no arm have no propensity score and are not judged by it.
.support <- ps_support(.ps_elig)$data
.elig$elig_propensity <- .elig$ID %in% .support[[ID]][!.support$weak_common]
.elig$elig_none <- TRUE
```

# Counts only. A row here would describe one patient, so the rows, with each patient's
# distance and the features behind it, stay in vt.rds under eligibility$rows.
.out <- .elig_rows[!.elig_rows$in_distribution, c("method", "arm")]
cat(nrow(.out), "patient-by-arm judgments are out of distribution; each is in `vt.rds`, under `eligibility$rows`.\n")
# Factors, so a job with no patient out of distribution still prints its table of zeros.
.ood_counts <- table(method = factor(.out$method, unique(.elig_rows$method)), arm = factor(.out$arm, unique(.elig_rows$arm)))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(.ood_counts, responseName = "patients"), row.names = FALSE)

```{r}
#| label: fig-ood

#|   within each panel. The dashed line is that arm's line, its largest nearest-neighbor gap among its own patients (for the
#|   isolation forest, the ISOLATION_CUTOFF quantile of its own scores): points above it are out of distribution."
.plot <- .elig_rows[is.finite(.elig_rows$distance), ]
.plot <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(split(.plot, list(.plot$method, .plot$arm), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
  x$rank <- rank(x$distance, ties.method = "first")

save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-eligibility")

```

#| tbl-cap: "Isolation forest: patients flagged against each arm at the cutoff in use and at the quantiles beside it"
# Only with "isolation" in ELIGIBILITY. The cutoff in use is ISOLATION_CUTOFF; the
# rest show how many patients sit between the lines, so a reader can see how much
# the eligible count depends on the choice.
if (is.null(.iso_sens)) {
  cat("The isolation forest is not among the ELIGIBILITY methods.\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(transform(.iso_sens, in_use = quantile == ISOLATION_CUTOFF), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

### Eligible, with a value the arm does not cover

Gower and the isolation forest each fold every eligibility variable into one
number, so one extreme value among many can leave a patient in distribution. The arm's forest
still extrapolates on that variable for them. These patients stay eligible;
this counts them for review, and a value outside the arm is often a data error
or a unit mix-up, worth checking against the chart.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-outside-range
#| tbl-cap: "Eligible patients with a value outside what the arm judged against shows, by variable"
# Counts only, as above. The arm's range or levels are not shown either: an age
# range can carry an age over 89, and a level an identifier. Each patient, with the
# value and the arm's range, is in vt.rds under eligibility$outside_range.
if (!nrow(.outside)) {
  cat("No eligible patient has a value outside the arm they were judged against.\n")
} else {
  .outside_counts <- stats::aggregate(ID ~ variable + arm + side, .outside, length)
  names(.outside_counts)[names(.outside_counts) == "ID"] <- "patients"
  knitr::kable(.outside_counts[order(.outside_counts$variable, .outside_counts$arm), ], row.names = FALSE)
}
```

### How far the rules overlap

Each rule asks the same question by a different route, and rules that answer it
alike flag the same patients. Where they flag different patients, the combined
rule depends on which were chosen, and so does the effect estimated on the
patients it keeps. The propensity rule (common support) is shown beside the
rules in `ELIGIBILITY` for comparison only; it judges treated patients alone.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-overlap
#| tbl-cap: "Patients by the rules that flag them, in each arm. A patient appears once, under the exact set of rules
#|   that flag them."
.rules <- c(stats::setNames(.methods, .methods), propensity = "propensity")
.flags <- as.data.frame(lapply(.rules, function(m) .elig[[paste0("elig_", m)]]))
.elig_arm <- .arm[match(.elig$ID, .ids)]
# A patient with no arm, or a treated patient the propensity model could not
# score (every eligibility variable missing), has no propensity score: not
# judged, rather than flagged. elig_propensity, vt-explain's sensitivity, still counts them ineligible.
.flags$propensity[is.na(.elig_arm) | !.elig$ID %in% .support[[ID]]] <- NA
.overlap <- vt_overlap(.flags, ifelse(is.na(.elig_arm), "No arm", .elig_arm))
knitr::kable(.overlap$combinations, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-agreement
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement between each pair of rules, over the patients both judged. Kappa is agreement beyond chance:
#|   1 is the same patients, 0 no more alike than chance."
knitr::kable(.overlap$pairs, row.names = FALSE)
```

## The arm forests

One survival forest per arm, grown on the patients who received that arm. A patient's own-arm curve
comes from their forest out of bag, so no one is predicted by trees grown on them.

```{r}
#| label: fit
#| message: true
CACHE_DIR <- dirname(set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))
.model <- stats::as.formula(paste0("Surv(", TIME, ", ", STATUS, ") ~ ", paste(.predictors, collapse = " + ")))
# The saved forest keeps this formula, and a formula keeps the environment it
# was made in, `job_data` and its patient IDs included. Point it at the global
# environment, which a saved file only refers to (rfs-fit does the same).
environment(.model) <- globalenv()
# The IDs of each forest's training rows, in training order. survival.oob rows
# follow this order, and vt_curves() matches on it rather than on d's order.
.train_ids <- stats::setNames(lapply(ARMS, function(a) d[[ID]][d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated]), ARMS)
.forests <- stats::setNames(lapply(ARMS, function(a) {
  da <- d[d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated, c(TIME, STATUS, .predictors), drop = FALSE]
  set.seed(SEED)
  cache_fit(paste0("vt-fit-", a),
            rfsrc(.model, data = da, ntree = NTREE, nsplit = NSPLIT, na.action = NA_ACTION,
                  importance = "none", block.size = 1, seed = -abs(SEED)),
            seed = SEED, dir = CACHE_DIR, refit = REFIT)
}), ARMS)
```

The C-index below is computed from each forest's out-of-bag predictions, not from the stored error rate
(which is not the C-index).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-performance
#| tbl-cap: "Each arm's forest, judged out of bag"
#| results: asis
.perf <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {
  f <- .forests[[a]]
  # yvar is the response as a data frame (time, status) for a survival forest.
  yt <- f$yvar[[1]]
  ys <- f$yvar[[2]]
  cc <- survival::concordance(survival::Surv(yt, ys) ~ f$predicted.oob, reverse = TRUE)
  se <- sqrt(cc$var)
  data.frame(arm = a, patients = f$n, events = sum(ys == 1), c_index = cc$concordance,
             lower = cc$concordance - 1.96 * se, upper = cc$concordance + 1.96 * se)
}))
cat(knitr::kable(.perf, digits = 3), sep = "\n")
.weak <- .perf$arm[which(.perf$lower <= 0.5)]
if (length(.weak)) {
  cat("\n**The interval for", paste(.weak, collapse = " and "), "includes 0.5.** That arm's half of every",
      "contrast below is exploratory.\n")
}
```

The C-index says whether a forest ranks patients; it says nothing about whether the survival it predicts
is the right level, and the RMST difference is a difference of levels. Calibration checks that: each
arm's patients are split into fifths by their out-of-bag predicted survival at the horizon, and each
fifth's mean prediction is set beside its Kaplan-Meier survival. A small arm can rank well and still be
far off here.

```{r}
#| label: calibration-helper
# Out-of-bag predicted survival at the horizon against Kaplan-Meier within
# groups of predicted survival, for one survival forest. survival.oob and yvar
# share the training order, so no matching by ID is needed. A patient never out
# of bag has no prediction and is left out, counted. A group whose follow-up
# ends before the horizon has no observed survival there: extending its curve
# would treat the last censored patients as immortal. It is NA, counted, unless
# the curve had already reached zero.
vt_calibration <- function(f, horizon, groups = 5L) {
  at <- findInterval(horizon, f$time.interest)
  pred <- if (at == 0L) rep(1, f$n) else f$survival.oob[, at]
  time <- f$yvar[[1]]
  status <- f$yvar[[2]]
  ok <- !is.na(pred)
  pred <- pred[ok]
  time <- time[ok]
  status <- status[ok]
  breaks <- unique(stats::quantile(pred, seq(0, 1, length.out = groups + 1L), names = FALSE))
  g <- if (length(breaks) > 1L) cut(pred, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) else rep(1L, length(pred))
  out <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(sort(unique(g)), function(k) {
    s <- g == k
    km <- summary(survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time[s], status[s]) ~ 1), times = horizon, extend = TRUE)
    observed <- if (length(km$surv)) km$surv else NA_real_
    if (max(time[s]) < horizon && !isTRUE(observed == 0)) observed <- NA_real_
    data.frame(group = k, patients = sum(s), events = sum(status[s] == 1), predicted = mean(pred[s]),
               observed = observed)
  }))
  attr(out, "no_prediction") <- sum(!ok)
  attr(out, "unsupported") <- sum(is.na(out$observed))
  out
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-calibration
#| tbl-cap: "Calibration at the horizon: each arm's patients in fifths of out-of-bag predicted survival, the
#|   fifth's mean prediction and its Kaplan-Meier survival"
#| results: asis
.cal <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(ARMS, function(a) {
  x <- vt_calibration(.forests[[a]], HORIZON)
  if (attr(x, "no_prediction")) {
    cat(attr(x, "no_prediction"), " ", a, " patient(s) were never out of bag and have no calibration prediction; ",
        "raise NTREE.\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  if (attr(x, "unsupported")) {
    cat(attr(x, "unsupported"), " ", a, " fifth(s) have no follow-up to ", HORIZON,
        " and no observed survival there; they are left out of the error.\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  cbind(arm = a, x)
}))
cat(knitr::kable(.cal, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE), sep = "\n")
# One number per arm: the mean distance between predicted and observed over the fifths, in percentage points.
.cal_error <- tapply(abs(.cal$predicted - .cal$observed), .cal$arm, mean, na.rm = TRUE)[ARMS]
cat("\nMean calibration error at ", HORIZON, ", in percentage points: ",
    paste0(ARMS, " ", format(round(100 * .cal_error, 1), nsmall = 1), collapse = ", "), ".\n", sep = "")
```

```{r}

#|   perfect agreement. Points below it: the forest predicts better survival than was observed."
.lim <- range(c(.cal$predicted, .cal$observed), na.rm = TRUE)
.fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(.cal[!is.na(.cal$observed), , drop = FALSE], ggplot2::aes(x = predicted, y = observed)) +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +

```

# What this report counts: patients and events by arm, the longest follow-up and the numbers at risk
# of the observed outcome, the patients each rule flags, and each calibration fifth's patients and

cat(hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_notice(rbind(

  hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_counts(.counts$Patients, "patients by arm"),

)))

## Twin curves

```{r}
#| label: curves-helper
# Two curves per patient. The arm a patient received comes from that arm's
# forest OUT OF BAG, so no one is predicted by trees grown on them. The other
# arm comes from predict() on the other forest. Rows with no arm get both from
# predict(). Everything is keyed by ID: predict() returns rows in the order it
# was given them, and pairing by position silently swaps patients. Under
# na.impute predict() imputes the new rows at random, so it takes the seed too.
# Each row also carries the forest's cumulative hazard, chf (chf.oob for the
# own arm), which the observed-against-expected test reads; it is not -log(surv),
# which is infinite where a forest's survival reaches 0. The handoff drops it.
vt_curves <- function(forests, train_ids, d, id, arm, arms, no_arm, seed) {
  out <- list()
  for (a in arms) {
    f <- forests[[a]]
    own <- d[[arm]] %in% a & !no_arm
    own_ids <- d[[id]][own]
    # survival.oob rows are in TRAINING order, which train_ids records; d may
    # be in any order, so each own-arm patient is matched to their row by ID.
    at <- match(own_ids, train_ids[[a]])
    if (anyNA(at)) stop(sum(is.na(at)), " arm ", a, " patient(s) are not among its forest's training rows.", call. = FALSE)
    oob <- f$survival.oob[at, , drop = FALSE]
    out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(ID = rep(own_ids, each = length(f$time.interest)), arm_of_curve = a,
                                          time = f$time.interest, surv = as.vector(t(oob)),
                                          chf = as.vector(t(f$chf.oob[at, , drop = FALSE])))
    other <- d[!own, , drop = FALSE]
    p <- predict(f, newdata = other[, f$xvar.names, drop = FALSE], na.action = "na.impute",
                 seed = seed)
    out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- data.frame(ID = rep(other[[id]], each = length(f$time.interest)), arm_of_curve = a,
                                          time = f$time.interest, surv = as.vector(t(p$survival)),
                                          chf = as.vector(t(p$chf)))
  }
  do.call(base::rbind, out)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: curves
.own_n <- vapply(ARMS, function(a) .forests[[a]]$n, integer(1L))
stopifnot(all(.own_n == lengths(.train_ids[ARMS])))
set.seed(SEED)
.curves <- vt_curves(.forests, .train_ids, d, ID, ARM, ARMS, no_arm = .no_arm, seed = -abs(SEED))
```

## The difference in restricted mean survival time

```{r}
#| label: rmst-helper
# RMST to the horizon: the area under a step survival curve, which starts at 1.
# The horizon must sit inside both arms' follow-up; past it every curve is cut
# at the same place and the difference is an artifact (a horizon in days on a
# fit in years gave identical curves once).
vt_rmst <- function(curves, horizon, arms, followup) {
  past <- names(followup)[followup < horizon]
  if (length(past)) {
    stop("HORIZON (", horizon, ") is beyond the largest follow-up time in arm(s) ", paste(past, collapse = ", "),
         " (", paste(signif(followup[past], 3), collapse = ", "), "). Check its units against TIME.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  # The risk is 1 - S(horizon), where S includes a step AT the horizon; the
  # area stops at the horizon, so a step there adds nothing to it.
  one <- function(t, s) {
    keep <- t < horizon
    knots <- c(0, t[keep], horizon)
    steps <- c(1, s[keep])
    at <- c(1, s[t <= horizon])
    c(rmst = sum(diff(knots) * steps), risk = 1 - utils::tail(at, 1L))
  }
  per <- lapply(split(curves, list(curves$ID, curves$arm_of_curve), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
    x <- x[order(x$time), ]
    v <- one(x$time, x$surv)
    data.frame(ID = x$ID[1L], arm_of_curve = x$arm_of_curve[1L], rmst = v[["rmst"]], risk = v[["risk"]])
  })
  long <- do.call(base::rbind, per)
  wide <- stats::reshape(long, idvar = "ID", timevar = "arm_of_curve", direction = "wide", sep = "_")
  wide$diff <- wide[[paste0("rmst_", arms[1])]] - wide[[paste0("rmst_", arms[2])]]
  # log_rr is +/-Inf or NaN when a patient's risk is 0 under an arm (vt-explain drops and counts those).
  wide$log_rr <- log(wide[[paste0("risk_", arms[1])]] / wide[[paste0("risk_", arms[2])]])
  rownames(wide) <- NULL
  wide
}
```

```{r}
#| label: rmst
.followup <- vapply(ARMS, function(a) max(d[[TIME]][d[[ARM]] %in% a & .treated]), numeric(1L))
.rmst <- vt_rmst(.curves, HORIZON, ARMS, .followup)
# no_arm marks the patients who received neither arm. Their arm is NA, never a label, so
# an arm that is really named "none" cannot be confused with them.
.rmst <- merge(data.frame(ID = d[[ID]], arm = ifelse(.no_arm, NA_character_, d[[ARM]]), no_arm = .no_arm),
               .rmst, by = "ID")
.rmst <- merge(.rmst, .elig, by = "ID")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-curves
#| fig-cap: "Mean predicted survival under each arm's forest, for patients in distribution, by the arm they received.
#|   The shaded area to the horizon is the restricted mean survival time."
.in_dist <- .rmst$ID[.rmst$elig]
if (!length(.in_dist)) {
  cat("No patient is in distribution under the combined rule; see the eligibility tables.\n")
} else {
  .mc <- .curves[.curves$ID %in% .in_dist, ]
  .at <- match(.mc$ID, .rmst$ID)
  .mc$received <- ifelse(.rmst$no_arm[.at], "No arm", .rmst$arm[.at])
  .mc <- stats::aggregate(surv ~ received + arm_of_curve + time, data = .mc, FUN = mean)
  # hv_rmst_curves() wants right-continuous steps that start at time 0 with surv 1.
  .mc <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(split(.mc, list(.mc$received, .mc$arm_of_curve), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
    base::rbind(data.frame(received = x$received[1L], arm_of_curve = x$arm_of_curve[1L], time = 0, surv = 1), x[order(x$time), ])
  }))
  .mc$facet <- paste("Received", .mc$received)
  .mc$arm <- .mc$arm_of_curve
  .fig <- plot(hvtiPlotR::hv_rmst_curves(.mc, tau = HORIZON, facet = "facet", arm = "arm")) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Time", y = "Mean predicted survival", color = "Curve under", fill = "Curve under")
  save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-curves")
  .fig
}
```

## Observed against expected

Two curves give no p-value. This section gives one: for each arm forest and each arm received, the
**deaths observed** against the **deaths the forest expects** for those same patients, each followed for as
long as they actually were. A patient's expected deaths are the forest's cumulative hazard at that
patient's own follow-up, read off its time grid as a step, and the group's are their sum, E. The ratio O/E,
its exact Poisson interval and the chi-squared test of O against E are the one-sample log-rank test
(Breslow 1975; Finkelstein, Muzikansky and Schoenfeld 2003). It is the test `hs-concordance` runs on hazard
models, through the same helper.

Five things to say beside the result:

- **Only the other arm's forest is tested.** The patients of arm B are not among arm A's forest's training
  rows, which this job checks by ID (`in_fit`), so their deaths against what arm A's forest expects for them
  is a test: the twins' counterfactual comparison as a count. A forest against its own arm is out of bag,
  so no patient is predicted by trees grown on them, but the other patients' deaths grew those trees and
  are in O too. O and E then depend on each other, and that cell is shown as a calibration of the forest,
  with no interval and no p-value.
- **Patients in distribution only**, as in the twin curves above: an out-of-distribution patient's
  other-arm prediction is an extrapolation.
- **The forest's own uncertainty is not in the test.** E is treated as fixed. A forest has no delta method,
  so adding it would mean bootstrapping the forests.
- **Follow-up stops at `TAU`.** Deaths and expectations are both counted to `TAU` and no further, and the
  figures stop there too.
- **The band is the spread of the patients' predictions**, their 15th to 85th percentiles, and not a
  confidence interval of anything. A forest gives no per-patient limits, so there is no average of them to
  draw, and the interval of the mean curve would need the bootstrap too.

```{r}
#| label: oe
#| results: asis
if (is.null(TAU)) TAU <- min(.followup)
if (!is.numeric(TAU) || length(TAU) != 1L || !is.finite(TAU) || TAU <= 0) {
  stop("TAU must be NULL or one positive number, in TIME's units.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (TAU > min(.followup)) {
  stop("TAU (", TAU, ") is beyond the follow-up of arm ", names(which.min(.followup)), " (",
       signif(min(.followup), 4), "). Leave TAU NULL to stop there.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (!is.numeric(SPAGHETTI_N) || length(SPAGHETTI_N) != 1L || !is.finite(SPAGHETTI_N) || SPAGHETTI_N < 1) {
  stop("SPAGHETTI_N must be one positive number.", call. = FALSE)
}
# The patients counted: treated and in distribution, by the arm they received.
.oe_pat <- data.frame(ID = d[[ID]], arm = d[[ARM]], time = d[[TIME]], event = d[[STATUS]])[.treated, , drop = FALSE]
.oe_pat <- .oe_pat[.oe_pat$ID %in% .rmst$ID[.rmst$elig], , drop = FALSE]
.oe_pat$t <- pmin(.oe_pat$time, TAU)
.oe_pat$ev <- as.integer(.oe_pat$event == 1 & .oe_pat$time <= TAU)

# One forest's curves for some patients, as patients x times matrices of survival
# and cumulative hazard, rows in the order of `ids`. .curves holds every patient
# under every forest on that forest's own grid.
.oe_matrix <- function(a, ids) {
  x <- .curves[.curves$arm_of_curve == a & .curves$ID %in% ids, , drop = FALSE]
  x <- x[order(match(x$ID, ids), x$time), , drop = FALSE]
  times <- .forests[[a]]$time.interest
  list(times = times, surv = matrix(x$surv, ncol = length(times), byrow = TRUE),
       chf = matrix(x$chf, ncol = length(times), byrow = TRUE), ids = unique(x$ID))
}

# One cell per arm forest and arm received.
.oe_cells <- list()
for (a in ARMS) for (g in ARMS) {
  p <- .oe_pat[.oe_pat$arm == g, , drop = FALSE]
  m <- .oe_matrix(a, p$ID)
  stopifnot(identical(m$ids, p$ID))
  # A patient never out of bag has no own-arm curve; they are left out and counted.
  ok <- stats::complete.cases(m$surv) & stats::complete.cases(m$chf)
  .oe_cells[[length(.oe_cells) + 1L]] <- list(model = a, group = g, ids = p$ID[ok], times = m$times,
                                              surv = m$surv[ok, , drop = FALSE], chf = m$chf[ok, , drop = FALSE],
                                              t = p$t[ok], ev = p$ev[ok], no_prediction = sum(!ok),
                                              in_fit = sum(p$ID %in% .train_ids[[a]]))
}
oe <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(.oe_cells, function(cell) {
  # Each patient's expected deaths: the forest's cumulative hazard at their own
  # follow-up, the step at or before it, and 0 before the forest's first time.
  k <- findInterval(cell$t, cell$times)
  h <- ifelse(k == 0L, 0, cell$chf[cbind(seq_along(k), pmax(k, 1L))])
  inference <- if (!length(h) || sum(h) <= 0) {
    "none: no patients or no expected deaths"
  } else if (cell$in_fit > 0L) {
    "none: these patients grew the forest (out of bag)"
  } else {
    "tested"
  }
  r <- if (startsWith(inference, "none: no patients")) {
    data.frame(n = length(h), observed = sum(cell$ev), expected = sum(h), ratio = NA_real_, lower = NA_real_,
               upper = NA_real_, level = TEST_LEVEL, chisq = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
  } else {
    hvtiRtemplates:::.one_sample_logrank(cell$ev, h, TEST_LEVEL)
  }
  if (inference != "tested") r[c("lower", "upper", "chisq", "p")] <- NA_real_
  data.frame(model = cell$model, group = cell$group, inference = inference, in_fit = cell$in_fit,
             no_prediction = cell$no_prediction, r)
}))
.cap_oe <- paste0("Observed against forest-expected deaths to ", signif(TAU, 4), ", by arm forest and arm received, ",
                  "patients in distribution, with ", 100 * TEST_LEVEL, "% intervals")
cat("Follow-up is counted to TAU = ", signif(TAU, 4), " (", TIME, "'s units); ", sum(.oe_pat$time > TAU),
    " patient(s) followed longer are censored there. ", sum(!.treated) + sum(!d[[ID]][.treated] %in% .oe_pat$ID),
    " patient(s) with no arm or out of distribution are not counted. Intervals are ", 100 * TEST_LEVEL, "%.\n",
    sep = "")
if (any(oe$no_prediction > 0L)) {
  cat("\n", sum(oe$no_prediction), " patient(s) were never out of bag and have no own-arm prediction; ",
      "raise NTREE.\n", sep = "")
}
# Cells of fewer than five patients or events, by count.
cat(hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_notice(rbind(
  hvtiRtemplates:::.identifiability_counts(c(oe$n, oe$observed, oe$n - oe$observed), "observed against expected")
)))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-oe
#| tbl-cap: !expr .cap_oe
knitr::kable(oe[c("model", "group", "inference", "in_fit", "n", "observed", "expected", "ratio", "lower", "upper",
                  "chisq", "p")], row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
```

### The average expected curve

Each forest's average expected curve is the mean of its patients' predicted survival on the forest's own
time grid to `TAU`, set against the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the same patients, with **95%** limits, beside
the test in each panel's title. The band is the 15th to 85th percentiles of the patients' predictions.

```{r}
#| label: oe-curves
oe_curves <- list()
.lines <- list()
# The band's label, for the caption, whichever cells have patients.
.band_label <- attr(hvtiRtemplates:::.cohort_curve_band(matrix(1), band = "spread"), "label")
for (cell in .oe_cells) {
  # A cell with no one in distribution has no curve; the table says so.
  if (!length(cell$ids)) next
  b <- hvtiRtemplates:::.cohort_curve_band(cell$surv, band = "spread")
  # The curve drawn must be the mean of the predictions the RMST table reads.
  # vt_rmst() takes each patient's survival at the horizon by its own path, so
  # a change to either would part them silently.
  at <- findInterval(HORIZON, cell$times)
  risk <- .rmst[[paste0("risk_", cell$model)]][match(cell$ids, .rmst$ID)]
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(if (at == 0L) 1 else b$mean[at], mean(1 - risk))))
  keep <- cell$times <= TAU
  panel <- local({
    r <- oe[oe$model == cell$model & oe$group == cell$group, , drop = FALSE]
    test <- if (r$inference != "tested") {
      paste0("O/E ", formatC(r$ratio, digits = 2, format = "f"), " (no test: ", sub("^none: ", "", r$inference), ")")
    } else {
      paste0("O/E ", formatC(r$ratio, digits = 2, format = "f"), " (", 100 * TEST_LEVEL, "% ",
             formatC(r$lower, digits = 2, format = "f"), " to ", formatC(r$upper, digits = 2, format = "f"),
             "), p ", format.pval(r$p, digits = 2, eps = 0.001))
    }
    paste0("received ", cell$group, ", ", cell$model, " forest\n", test)
  })
  oe_curves[[length(oe_curves) + 1L]] <- data.frame(model = cell$model, group = cell$group, panel = panel,
                                                    time = c(0, cell$times[keep]), mean = c(1, b$mean[keep]),
                                                    lower = c(1, b$lower[keep]), upper = c(1, b$upper[keep]))
  # The spaghetti's patients: all of them, or SPAGHETTI_N spaced evenly through
  # the ranking of survival at the last time drawn, so the thinned lines keep the spread.
  last <- max(1L, sum(keep))
  pick <- order(cell$surv[, last])
  if (length(pick) > SPAGHETTI_N) pick <- pick[unique(round(seq(1, length(pick), length.out = SPAGHETTI_N)))]
  .lines[[length(.lines) + 1L]] <- data.frame(panel = panel, patient = rep(pick, each = sum(keep) + 1L),
                                              time = c(0, cell$times[keep]),
                                              surv = as.vector(t(cbind(1, cell$surv[pick, keep, drop = FALSE]))))
}
oe_curves <- do.call(base::rbind, oe_curves)
.lines <- do.call(base::rbind, .lines)
# The Kaplan-Meier of each arm received, to TAU as the test counts it, one copy
# per panel. A limit survfit() leaves undefined stays NA and is not drawn.
.oe_km <- do.call(base::rbind, lapply(Filter(function(cell) length(cell$ids) > 0L, .oe_cells), function(cell) {
  step <- hvtiRtemplates:::.km_steps(cell$t, cell$ev, 0.95)
  step$panel <- unique(oe_curves$panel[oe_curves$model == cell$model & oe_curves$group == cell$group])
  step
}))
.oe_km_band <- .oe_km[!is.na(.oe_km$lower) & !is.na(.oe_km$upper), , drop = FALSE]
.cap_oe_km <- paste0("Kaplan-Meier survival of each arm received, with 95% limits, against the average survival each ",
                     "arm forest expects for the same patients. Band: ", .band_label, ".")
.cap_spaghetti <- paste0("Each patient's predicted survival (thin lines; at most ", SPAGHETTI_N, " per panel, spaced ",
                         "evenly through the ranking at the last time) and their average (heavy line).")
.npanel <- length(unique(oe_curves$panel))
.oe_none <- "No patient is in distribution under the combined rule, so there is no curve to draw.\n"
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-expected-km
#| fig-cap: !expr .cap_oe_km
if (!.npanel) {
  cat(.oe_none)
} else {
  .cols <- hvtiRtemplates:::.group_colors(c("Kaplan-Meier", "Expected"))
  .fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = .data$time)) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = .oe_km_band, ggplot2::aes(ymin = 100 * .data$lower, ymax = 100 * .data$upper,
                                                          fill = "Kaplan-Meier"), alpha = 0.15) +
    ggplot2::geom_path(data = .oe_km, ggplot2::aes(y = 100 * .data$surv, color = "Kaplan-Meier")) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = oe_curves, ggplot2::aes(ymin = 100 * .data$lower, ymax = 100 * .data$upper,
                                                        fill = "Expected"), alpha = 0.25) +
    ggplot2::geom_step(data = oe_curves, ggplot2::aes(y = 100 * .data$mean, color = "Expected"), linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = .cols, name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = .cols, name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Time", y = "Survival (%)") +
    hvtiPlotR::theme_hv_manuscript(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
  save_figure(.fig, "vt-fit-expected-km", width = 6.5, height = min(9, 1 + 2.75 * ceiling(.npanel / 2)))
  .fig
}
```

## Handoff

```{r}
#| label: save
# The product of this job, and what vt-explain reads, in one file so its parts
# cannot drift apart. The forests are kept so vt-explain grows none.
vt_handoff <- hvtiRtemplates:::.attach_handoff_lineage(
  list(rmst = .rmst, curves = .curves[c("ID", "arm_of_curve", "time", "surv")], forests = .forests, oe = oe,
       eligibility = list(rows = .elig_rows, methods = .methods, combine = COMBINE, sid_set = SID_SET, ordinal = ORDINAL,
                          variables = .elig_vars, sid_variables = .sid_vars, ps = .ps,
                          isolation = list(cutoff = ISOLATION_CUTOFF, sensitivity = .iso_sens), age_cap = AGE_CAP,
                          outside_range = .outside),
       predictors = list(names = .predictors, vp_set = VP_SET),
       settings = list(performance = .perf, calibration = .cal, arms = ARMS, horizon = HORIZON, tau = TAU, test_level = TEST_LEVEL,
                       ntree = NTREE, seed = SEED,
                       time = TIME, status = STATUS,
                       id = ID, id_key = hvtiRtemplates:::.id_key_fingerprint(.id_key),
                       arm = ARM, imputation = IMPUTATION, imputation_use = IMPUTATION_USE,
                       imputation_m = if (!is.null(IMPUTATION)) .m,
                       # Everything read_job_data() was given, so vt-explain reads the same patients and values.
                       read = list(dataset = DATASET, analysis_set = ANALYSIS_SET, where = WHERE, key = KEY,
                                   join = JOIN, join_vars = JOIN_VARS, reduce = REDUCE, join_key = JOIN_KEY))),
  # .provenance_data already holds the vp and sid sets' data lineage (appended
  # where each was read); their handoff records go in as artifacts.
  data = .provenance_data,
  artifacts = c(list(), if (!is.null(.vp_read)) c(.vp_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.vp_read$record)),
                if (!is.null(.sid_read)) c(.sid_read$lineage$artifacts, list(.sid_read$record))),
  analysis = list(time = list(variable = TIME), event = list(variable = STATUS, event = 1L, censored = 0L)),
  selection = attr(job_data$record, "selection")
)
saveRDS(vt_handoff, set_path("estimates", "vt.rds"))
```
